page.layout: One page of text in a single column; in the right margin, notes beside the lines of the lower part (marked II., Pelagiana & Semipelagiana, and the catchword-area mark B at the foot). Page number at the head centre.

main_text.p: voluntas Dei est prima causa omniū: ( Facit enim Deus omnia, de consilio voluntatis suæ. Eph. 1. v. 11.) quid absurdi est, statuere, quòd divina voluntas prius vult res esse, quàm suus intellectus judicet, res fore. Neque enim ideò vult Deus, quia prævidit futuras, sive velit, sive nolit: ( nihil enim futurum est, nisi ipsius voluntate prægressâ, ut causâ futurorum ) sed, quia vult, futuræ sunt.

Atque ita hæc Scylla, quæ putatur, & revera non est, declinata est: ideoque nihil hîc metuendum periculi, ubi omnia ( uti partim jam vidimus; partim amplius videre est apud nostros doctores, & ipsū etiam Augustinum, Prosperum, aliosque Patres ) planissimis Scripturæ dictis constant.

Ex altera verò parte, non solùm periculosa est illa Charybdis, in Pelagianismo & Semipelagianismo, quæ refertur verbis synodi Arausicanæ secundæ ( Nullam esse humanæ naturæ depravationem: Gratiam ad solā remissione peccatorum valere, &c.) damnata Synodis compluribus, quarum nūm II. Pelagiana & Semipelagiana.

page.notes: Right-margin notes read "II." and "Pelagiana & Semipelagiana"; the mark at the foot is a signature-type letter "B" and is given as a foot line. Line ends "nūm" at the foot of the page is cut off by the page edge and may continue on the next page. Lines of the first paragraph with the word "quod" appear as "quòd"; the scan is slightly blurred in the lower third, so the reading of "Synodis compluribus" and "Scripturae dictis" is uncertain. Several words in the Scylla sentence (e.g. "putatur", "declinata") are only moderately clear.
